blinding_guess.why: On the provided side the emitted call_service (args = extracted dict) and service_response (values = dict on success, str(exc) on failure) match the in-snapshot protocol spec, and advertise.latch/queue_size and subscribe.queue_length are all read with the spec defaults. The one inconsistency seen is on the inbound path of service_response.values: the ServiceResponse capability type-checks values as dict and always reads message["values"] ignoring result, while the spec allows a string or absent values when result is false. Whether that counts for the listed provides-side element is unclear.

notes: The elements are rosbridge JSON protocol operations (op codes) and their fields, not ROS IDL types. msg_type uses the packet's rosbridge_protocol/<op> naming. The code names the operations by op string (register_operation / "op" literals). No .msg/.srv/.action/.idl definition exists for them in the snapshot, and ros_distro is null, so definition_id is null for every port and the msg declares entries carry null in the hash slot. Their field types are taken from the prose definition tables in ROSBRIDGE_PROTOCOL.md (protocol v2.0.0, line 1). Side mapping: the package emits call_service to clients that advertised a service (advertise_service.py:57-63) and emits service_response after proxying a client's call (call_service.py:141-163). It also accepts both ops inbound (CallService capability consumes call_service.args as list or dict, services.py:121-125; ServiceResponse capability consumes service_response.values as dict, service_response.py:16,37), but these are not listed in references because the packet assigns them the provides side. QoS is null on all ports because the ports are WebSocket/JSON protocol messages, not DDS entities. For context, the ROS entities these fields configure are: advertise creates a publisher with QoSProfile(depth=queue_size, durability=TRANSIENT_LOCAL) whatever latch is; latch=false adds lifespan 1 s; latch=true sets depth=1 and no lifespan (publishers.py:125-136). Reliability is not set in code; the spec documents reliable (ROSBRIDGE_PROTOCOL.md:236). subscribe creates a subscription with depth=10 and VOLATILE/BEST_EFFORT by default. It switches to TRANSIENT_LOCAL+RELIABLE when all discovered publishers are transient local, and to BEST_EFFORT when any discovered publisher is best effort (subscribers.py:137-151). That choice depends on discovered peers, so it is not statically determined. subscribe.queue_length is not a QoS depth: it sizes rosbridge's outbound throttle queue (deque maxlen, subscription_modifiers.py:127), and the minimum is taken across a client's subscriptions to one topic (subscribe.py:220). Unlike the publish op (publish.py:51-52), the advertise op does not type-check latch or queue_size (advertise.py:103). Defaults in code: latch False, queue_size 100, queue_length 0, call_service timeout default_call_service_timeout 5.0. The glob permission parameters default to "" (no restriction) and are read at run time. exclusive is empty: no hardware command interface or device handle is claimed; the WebSocket listening port (param port, default 9090) is bound with bind_sockets but is not recorded as an exclusive device resource. All seven package.xml files in the snapshot are version 4.0.0; manifest_version is taken from the rosbridge_suite metapackage.
